I am a man of the Moselle who can never, for all eternity, be canalized—and who is therefore cursed by the Pope with every ban and anathema.

They took the chalice away from the laity, and in doing so they lost control over the intoxicants. Now they are dying miserably because of it. And they need the wretched Adolf as a bogeyman so that they can fraternize with the Jews, who for their part have needed such bogeymen for two thousand years in order to raise their own moral standing and collect compensation as victims—provided they can find fools to pay it: reparations, that is.
Inside Germany this is comparatively easy. Outside Germany it is difficult. And for that they need Germany again. Hence this compulsion.

The first greeting of the New Year was miching mallecho: a radio talk by Hermann Heimpel on NWDR calling on us to repent and make reparations, and warning us not to forget that we are criminals while the others, who are entitled to compensation, are the victims of our crimes.
A quotation from [Franz] Böhm revealed the heart of the matter.
Keep stirring up our sense of guilt, and paying will become easier for us!
Joyfully we pay our billions as we hear repentance’s minstrels.

Before this Shylock greeting came my reading of the new Catholic catechism for West Germany. It is no longer “the Jews” who crucified our Lord and Savior. That no longer appears in the Roman catechism. Instead it was:
What exactly is worse for us now?
Sovereign is he who decides on the state of exception.
How cheerfully I crowed that definition of sovereignty out into the world back in 1921!
And how right I turned out to be.
Today everyone quotes it who suffers under somebody else’s sovereignty, while everyone who exercises sovereignty himself suppresses it and keeps silent about it.
Today I know that Hans Freyer is right when he says, in his Theory of the Present Age of 1955:
Exceptions do not count; they are charged against the person who points them out.
Does anyone apart from me have any idea how magnificent it is?
Anyone apart from me, the victim of precisely this reality?
For that reason alone I want to travel to Wiesbaden tomorrow to speak with Hans Freyer.
The concrete exception can arise in two opposite directions and from two opposite impulses.
Grace comes from an abundance of security and gives its goodness without needing a reason.
Dictatorship comes from a lack of security and can no longer be good, because it feels threatened by a dangerous enemy. That is the polarity between grace and dictatorship.
No one thinks about this. Even Wilhelm Grewe failed to recognize the passage from 1921 in the introductory note to my book on dictatorship, p. IX.
That would probably have been asking too much.
The one drips like heaven’s gentle rain; The other drops hydrogen-bomb blessings.
The difference between goodness and anxiety.
Agnosticism produces anxiety rather than fear; means of annihilation rather than weapons.
The great man, the magnus homo, is a great father, or a great brother, or else a great beast—namely Leviathan.
We cannot do without such enlargements.
Question: is the great mother still the great human being?
Or must greatness take the form of a great man?
Only in the masculine does this upward intensification lead to the hero, to the lord, and to rule.
The great mother is only a great womb.
The great man drops bombs upon the small; Thus mankind makes itself one whole. It need only negate the other’s No, And everyone will think the same.
In January 1956 the GDR—the German Democratic Republic—introduced a criminal prohibition, a law threatening with death the crime of Abwerbung, enticing or recruiting people away.
Automobilism; car traps; alcohol consumption; aggressive war; and now: enticing people away.
After all, a manufacturer once poached my cleaning woman.
Young Paris poached beautiful Helen from old Menelaus. And the Russians poached several Nobel Prize winners and atomic physicists from the Americans, and they were certainly no Helens.
Naturally these are all crimes for which the abolished death penalty must immediately be brought back.
To the right of the right-hand clipping:

And here, ladies and gentlemen, you have one-hundred-percent potestas indirecta, indirect power, to which nothing can ever happen because it will certainly end up on the side of the victor, no matter what that victor looks like. For the Christian-social ideal is the victorious war won by other people, after which one joins the victor. And if, while exercising our divine right to political error, we should happen to bet even slightly on the wrong side, we afterwards swing ourselves all the more energetically onto the victor’s side. There are victors, and there are those who belong with the victors.
We, at any rate, always belong to those who belong.
So listen <…> to this supremely legitimized representative of potestas indirecta:
“The Pope too has a right to a private life; and the public has a right to learn about this private life—insofar as it is edifying.”
I will be very careful not to tell you.
Besides, you should be ashamed of yourself for asking me.
All your questions and questionnaires are overflowing with time and temporality.
Answer to my persecutors E. Kaufmann, Fr. Böhm, Küster, W. Strauss, and Ebenstein:
Rabies is the accusation the dog brings against its master.
Do you know who said that?
But how could these poor dogs know such a thing?!
Shame on you for asking them.
Hail to me that I saw the great departures and those who broke them open!
The German language keeps releasing new ironic creations from the abyss of its profundity.
The latest examples: the European civil servant; the integration employee; the Western senior government councillor.
One only has to ask what all of this is called in French, and then in English, and the whole West is exposed as a piece of suburban Bonn magic.

Meanwhile, of course—as for me, in the old way—meanwhile several solid bourgeois families have thoroughly “consolidated” themselves. That is: they have scraped together something “under their feet,” some real estate, and had it entered in the land register. And so, if anyone dares to challenge this profit—their strictly legal profit—the matter becomes a problem of the constitutional state itself: first, law; second, state.

So, for the sake of dear peace, let us grant the whole Holy Family all its plots of land, buildings, investments, shares, securities, and pensions that it carried away as the final result of its heroic struggle against the miserable criminal Hitler.
May they live on them for a long time!
